question: What is the main purpose of a home visit in community nursing?

options.A: To perform major surgical procedures at home
options.B: To assess the financial status of the family
options.C: To provide care in the patient's natural environment

explanation: Home visits bring healthcare directly to where patients live so nurses can see their everyday environment and support them there. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is seeing a patient at home more revealing than seeing them in a hospital clinic?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any health teaching
options.B: It gives the nurse access to advanced laboratory equipment
options.C: It shows their true daily living conditions and family dynamics
options.D: It forces the patient to follow medical advice strictly

explanation: The home environment exposes real-life challenges like food storage, safety hazards, and family support systems that clinics hide. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h1)

question: What is the purpose of the clean apron inside the home visiting kit?

options.A: To protect the nurse's uniform from contamination
options.B: To dry the patient's hands after washing
options.C: To serve as a clean bandage for large wounds
options.D: To keep the nurse warm in cold weather

explanation: The apron acts as a barrier between the nurse's clothes and the patient's immediate surroundings during care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h2)

question: Why must every item inside the home visiting kit have a specific, designated place?

options.A: To ensure the patient can easily borrow the tools
options.B: To comply with fashion standards for community nurses
options.C: To make the bag heavier and more professional looking
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination and save time during emergencies

explanation: Organizing the bag strictly separates clean items from used ones, stopping the spread of germs while keeping care efficient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h2)

question: How is the outside of the home visiting bag treated during a visit?
explanation: The outside of the bag touches various surfaces during travel and home entry, so it is always treated as contaminated. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: What should the nurse do immediately after using an instrument during a home visit?

options.A: Return it straight into the clean section of the bag
options.B: Give it to the family members to wash later
options.C: Place it on the bare floor next to the patient's bed
options.D: Keep it separated and clean it before storing it away

explanation: Used equipment must never mix with clean supplies and requires proper cleaning and disinfection before going back into the bag. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: When should the nurse wash their hands during a home visit bag procedure?

options.A: Right after placing the bag on the floor
options.B: Only if the patient asks for hand sanitization
options.C: Only after finishing all tasks and leaving the house
options.D: Before opening the bag and handling clean equipment

explanation: Hand hygiene is performed before touching clean kit items to avoid transferring germs from the outside world onto sterile or clean supplies. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h4)

question: A nurse arrives at a patient's home for a dressing change. What is the very first action the nurse should take regarding the visiting kit?

options.A: Ask the patient to wash the stethoscope with soap
options.B: Place a protective paper lining on a surface and set the bag on it
options.C: Put the used dressing materials directly inside the main bag
options.D: Open the bag and pull out the forceps immediately

explanation: Setting down a protective barrier before placing the bag protects the kit from picking up contamination from furniture or tables. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to dispose of used injection needles during a home visit?

options.A: Putting them in a puncture-resistant safety box
options.B: Placing them in a designated sharps container
options.C: Throwing them loosely into the family's household trash can
options.D: Returning them securely to the health clinic

explanation: Loose needles in household trash pose a serious needle-stick injury risk to family members and waste handlers. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why is strict waste segregation vital during home visits?

options.A: It prevents the spread of infection to the family and community
options.B: It eliminates the need for hand washing after care
options.C: It makes the nurse finish the visit much faster
options.D: It reduces the total weight of the home visiting kit bag

explanation: Separating infectious and hazardous waste stops germs from spreading into the local environment and harming others. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h5)

question: When should used items in the home visiting kit be restocked?

options.A: Immediately after returning to the health clinic
options.B: Just before walking into the next patient's house
options.C: Only when a supervisor inspects the bag
options.D: Once every three to six months

explanation: Restocking right after returning ensures the nurse is always prepared for sudden emergency calls without delays. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h6)

question: What is the main risk of failing to regularly check expiration dates on kit supplies?

options.A: Using expired items that may be ineffective or unsafe for patients
options.B: Changing the color of the bag's inner lining
options.C: Attracting household insects to the storage locker
options.D: Making the visiting bag too heavy to carry comfortably

explanation: Expired antiseptics or sterile materials can lose their potency or harbor contamination, endangering patient safety. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h6)
